name: Abul Hashim
contribution: As general secretary of the Bengal Provincial Muslim League from 1943, Abul Hashim helped reorganise the party and expand its support among Bengali Muslims before the 1946 election.
context: He combined Muslim League politics with a regional Bengali emphasis and, during the 1946-47 partition debate, supported proposals for an independent and undivided Bengal.
impact: His career shows that Muslim politics in late-colonial Bengal was not a single-position movement: arguments for Pakistan coexisted with competing visions of Bengali regional sovereignty and identity.
seoDescription: Profile of Abul Hashim, tracing connections to the 1947 Partition, Eastern Bengal, and related political-cultural history.
shortAnswer: Abul Hashim is linked to the 1947 Partition in this timeline as Bengal Muslim League Organizer.

faq.question: How is Abul Hashim connected to the 1947 Partition?
faq.answer: Abul Hashim was general secretary of the Bengal Provincial Muslim League and later supported the proposal for an independent, undivided Bengal during the 1946-47 partition debate. His role helps explain the competing political projects present in late-colonial Bengal.
